links.outcome: Human annotation error rates by multi-LLM agreement stratum, and error detection AUC
links.effect: Human error rates rose from 0% at scores 3–4 to 76% at score 0; lowest-agreement stratum was 6.5% of annotations but held ~80% of errors; AUC-ROC 0.991, AUC-PR 0.893.
links.quote: Human error rates rose as LLM agreement fell, from 0% at scores 3–4 to 76% at score 0.

links.outcome: Ability of multi-LLM disagreement to flag erroneous human annotations versus blinded reviewer adjudication
links.effect: Prevalence-adjusted AUC-ROC 0.991 (95% CI 0.987–0.994) and AUC-PR 0.893 (95% CI 0.851–0.929) for error detection; outperformed single models.
links.quote: The multi-LLM disagreement score achieved a prevalence-adjusted AUC-ROC of 0.991 (95% CI 0.987–0.994) and AUC-PR of 0.893 (95% CI 0.851–0.929) for error detection.
